name: Confluence
tagline: A team knowledge and documentation workspace to evaluate for durable, searchable operational knowledge.
description: Confluence is a team documentation workspace to evaluate for shared knowledge, project context and internal procedures. Fit depends on information architecture, permissions, search, integrations, content lifecycle and how the team keeps documentation current.
pros: Structured spaces and pages can give teams a shared place for decisions and procedures.
A realistic search task can test whether employees can find trusted information.
Templates and ownership rules can support repeatable documentation.
cons: Documentation becomes stale without clear owners and review dates.
Permissions and external sharing require careful governance.
Migration and export need to preserve links, attachments and page context.

content.title: Information architecture
content.body: Create a small set of spaces based on the audience and purpose, not the org chart alone. Define page templates, naming conventions, labels and ownership. Test whether a new teammate can find a policy, a project decision and a runbook without asking an expert.

content.title: Search and content lifecycle
content.body: Run realistic searches using the words staff actually use. Check duplicate pages, stale instructions and conflicting answers. Assign an owner and review date to important pages and define how superseded content is marked without breaking useful references.

content.title: Permissions and collaboration
content.body: Test editing, comments, restricted pages and guest access using accounts from different roles. Confirm that sensitive HR, customer or security documents are not visible to unintended groups. Review account offboarding and external-sharing settings.

content.title: Integration and migration
content.body: Test links and context with the tools used for tasks, code, service requests and chat. Export a sample space with attachments and verify how links, page history and permissions translate. Document what cannot be migrated automatically.

content.title: Adoption and total cost
content.body: Measure whether the workspace reduces repeated questions and makes decisions easier to retrieve. Include page cleanup, migration, templates, training, administration and plan-specific permissions in the cost model. Verify current product limits directly.

content.title: Pilot acceptance criteria
content.body: Ask a new employee to find the current onboarding steps, a project decision and an operational runbook. Measure whether they find the right page without guidance and whether the page identifies an owner and review date. Record duplicate or contradictory pages that need cleanup.

content.title: Failure cases and governance
content.body: Test a restricted page, an external guest, a former employee and a page that has been superseded. Confirm access and link behavior. Decide who reviews critical documentation and how old instructions are marked so users do not follow stale processes.

content.title: Decision record
content.body: Document space structure, content owners, permission groups, templates, search expectations, migration scope and export needs. Compare the time required to keep information current with the benefit of making it discoverable. Confirm current plan controls before storing sensitive information.

faqs.question: Who should evaluate Confluence?
faqs.answer: Evaluate Confluence when its primary workflow matches a documented requirement. Run a representative pilot and verify current capabilities, limits and contract terms directly with the vendor.

faqs.question: Are prices and ratings independently verified here?
faqs.answer: No. This review does not present an independently verified price or third-party rating. Check current official documentation and obtain a dated quote.

faqs.question: What should a pilot include?
faqs.answer: Test the main workflow, one failure case, permissions, integrations, export and offboarding. Record pass, partial pass, fail or unknown and assign an owner to every unresolved requirement.

faqs.question: How should total cost be compared?
faqs.answer: Include licenses, usage, implementation, migration, training, integrations, support, internal administration and renewal terms—not only the headline subscription.

author: Sarah Chen
learningCurve: Steep — requires dedicated training time for full proficiency
whoShouldUse: Confluence is ideal for small to mid-size teams that need a reliable project management solution without excessive complexity. It works well for organizations with 5-200 users who prioritize ease of use and quick deployment.
whoShouldNotUse: Confluence may be overwhelming for users who only need basic project management functionality. Its extensive feature set can create unnecessary complexity for simple use cases.
